tldr_label: TL;DR: The S&P 500 and Dow enter correction as Nvidia faces an SEC probe, NATO calls Russia's missile breach of Poland a grave violation, and COP31 runs into ov

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3% on Friday. The S&P and Dow closed about 10% below their records, and the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gain. [[TAG:danger:correction]]

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Nvidia fell about 14% after Reuters reported the SEC is examining its accounting. Anthropic shares came within cents of their $83 IPO price before recovering. [[TAG:danger:SEC probe]]

tldr_bullets.label: Poland
tldr_bullets.body: NATO called Russian missiles landing in Poland a grave violation, Tusk called it an apparent intentional provocation, and Rutte is due in Warsaw today. [[TAG:warning:NATO soil]]

tldr_bullets.label: Washington
tldr_bullets.body: Back from Asia, Trump praised Xi and Putin as friends at a 90-minute press conference but offered little new on Ukraine. [[TAG:info:few results]]

tldr_bullets.label: Climate
tldr_bullets.body: COP31 went into overtime with no political deal after a draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels. [[TAG:warning:overtime]]

sections.title: Markets: Into Correction
sections.summary: S&P 500 drops 3.7% for a seventh loss; Nasdaq wipes out its 2026 gain

paragraphs.heading: Friday's Rout
paragraphs.body: UPI reported that the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 on Friday, its seventh straight loss, closing more than 10% below its October record. The Dow fell 949.73 points to 48,147.33 and also entered a correction. The Nasdaq composite dropped 5.3% to 22,617.73, and NBC News and CNBC reported it erased its 2026 gain. [[TAG:danger:seventh loss]]

paragraphs.heading: Worst Week
paragraphs.body: Cappnotes reported that the S&P 500 lost 8.6% for the week, its worst since April 2025, while the Nasdaq fell about 10%. The Inquirer and Axios tied the selloff to accelerating losses in AI stocks, with Axios noting that Anthropic's debut failed to halt the slide. Stockinvest reported chip stocks led the decline. [[TAG:danger:AI repricing]]

paragraphs.heading: Bonds and the Fed
paragraphs.body: FXStreet reported that the 10-year Treasury yield slipped below 5% as investors moved from stocks into bonds, even as Fed minutes showed nearly all policymakers expected further rate increases. Kitco reported that gold and silver also fell as investors cut risk, and that Brent settled at $92.57.

sections.title: Nvidia and Anthropic: AI Under Pressure
sections.summary: SEC reportedly probes Nvidia accounting; Anthropic tests its $83 IPO price

paragraphs.heading: Nvidia Probe
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg and The Daily Star, citing Reuters, reported that SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at Nvidia. Reuters could not determine when the probe began or which issues are under review, and Nvidia did not immediately comment. Motley Fool said the stock just had its worst week in 18 years. Crypto Briefing dated the start of reporting on the probe to November 17, which does not match other accounts. [[TAG:warning:unconfirmed scope]]

paragraphs.heading: Anthropic Day Two
paragraphs.body: Yahoo Finance reported that Anthropic fell as low as $83.05 on its second trading day, five cents above its IPO price, then closed at $88.30. Other reports put the close at $88.91, so the exact figure is unsettled. MLQ reported that the greenshoe option lifted the total raise to $93.5 billion. Motley Fool tied the decline to the broader AI selloff rather than company news. [[TAG:warning:near IPO price]]

sections.title: Poland: NATO Responds
sections.summary: NATO calls missile breach a grave violation; Warsaw seeks more air defenses

paragraphs.heading: The Breach
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Tusk called the landing of Russian missiles on Polish soil an apparent intentional provocation, during an attack that killed at least eight people in Ukraine. PBS reported that NATO called it a grave violation of Polish airspace. Bytes Europe reported that Poland requested additional NATO air defenses. [[TAG:warning:provocation]]

paragraphs.heading: What Next
paragraphs.body: Reports said Rutte is due in Warsaw on Saturday. Al Jazeera reported that analysts see direct Russia-NATO confrontation as unlikely, with Article 4 consultations a possible step. Nacionale reported it was not yet clear whether Poland would formally request Article 4 talks. Kyiv Post reported that European leaders condemned the breach and pledged support for Poland. [[TAG:info:Rutte in Warsaw]]

sections.title: Washington: Trump Reports Back
sections.summary: Trump praises Xi and Putin as friends; little new on Ukraine or concessions

paragraphs.heading: The Press Conference
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that Trump spent much of a 90-minute news conference praising Xi and Putin and defended his relationship with Putin after Russia's large attack on Ukraine. CBS News reported that he touted Asia deals. GPB said the trip offered few signs that either leader would make significant concessions. [[TAG:info:little substance]]

paragraphs.heading: Peace Track
paragraphs.body: CNN and NBC News had earlier reported Zelensky's account that US negotiators floated Ukraine ceding parts of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, which he refused. Al Jazeera noted that NATO accession requires unanimous approval by members. No new terms were reported this week. [[TAG:warning:unresolved]]

sections.sources: CNN, CBS News, GPB, NBC News, Al Jazeera

sections.title: Gulf: Mines and Blockade
sections.summary: IRGC reports more tanker mine strikes; experts doubt the scale of the threat

paragraphs.heading: Tanker Claims
paragraphs.body: Middle East Eye and TRT World reported IRGC statements that more oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Daily Times reported another strike on Saturday. These accounts come mainly from the IRGC and have not been independently confirmed. ABC News reported that Trump said Iran does not want a deal acceptable to him. [[TAG:warning:IRGC claims]]

paragraphs.heading: Skepticism
paragraphs.body: The National reported that experts say Iran is exaggerating the sea mine threat to tighten its grip on the strait. It quoted Intertanko as saying it does not believe mines pose a risk to shipping, and noted that US Central Command says primary routes have been cleared. [[TAG:info:disputed]]

sections.title: COP31: Overtime
sections.summary: Antalya talks extended with no political deal; fossil fuel language still the fight

paragraphs.heading: Extended
paragraphs.body: Hurriyet Daily News reported that COP31 was extended after countries failed to conclude negotiations on finance, emissions, adaptation and a just transition, and that a late session approved only technical matters. The Manila Times, carrying UN News, reported that countries are demanding a stronger deal. Time News reported that the talks entered their final hours with no agreement on fossil fuels. [[TAG:warning:no deal yet]]

paragraphs.heading: Side Deals
paragraphs.body: Sight Magazine reported that the conference delivered investment deals for host Turkey even as climate diplomacy stalled. World Today News reported that fossil fuel references had been removed from the draft. A further draft was expected on Saturday.

sections.title: Also Watching
sections.summary: Gaza offensive ends; Israel unity talks Sunday; Horn of Africa and Japan-China strains

paragraphs.heading: Gaza and Israel
paragraphs.body: Anadolu reported that Israel ended its central Gaza offensive on Thursday, leaving widespread destruction, and Middle East Monitor reported one Palestinian killed and 13 injured on Friday. The Times of Israel and the Jerusalem Post reported no progress so far in unity talks between Eisenkot's bloc and Likud, and Yahoo reported Eisenkot saying he will form a minority government if needed. [[TAG:warning:truce strained]]

paragraphs.heading: Horn of Africa
paragraphs.body: TimesLive, carrying Reuters, reported that Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their border, while NBC News reported that Ethiopia and Sudan accuse each other of backing armed fighters. Eritrea denies incursions. [[TAG:danger:war risk]]

paragraphs.heading: Japan and China
paragraphs.body: Nikkei Asia reported that Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said Japan's position on Taiwan remains unchanged, and Latin Times reported that tensions blocked a formal meeting with Xi in Shenzhen. JKN reported that Beijing is pressing her to retract her Taiwan remarks.
